title: Functorial Picard obstruction for square-zero thickenings of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $X_0\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over a scheme, defined by a quasi-coherent ideal $J$ with $J^2=0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Regard $J$ as an $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module. Here quasi-coherent means that restriction to every affine etale chart is the sheaf associated with a module. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(Y)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of line modules on $Y$ under tensor product [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $H^q(Y,F)$ for the right derived global sections of the additive sheaf underlying the $\mathcal O_Y$-module $F$ on the small etale site. There is a canonical group homomorphism $\delta_X:\operatorname{Pic}(X_0)\to H^2(X_0,J)$ with $\ker\delta_X=\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X_0))$. For any commutative square of square-zero closed immersions $Y_0\hookrightarrow Y$ and $X_0\hookrightarrow X$, with vertical maps $h_0:Y_0\to X_0$ and $h:Y\to X$, let $K$ be the ideal on $Y_0$. The structure maps give a coefficient map $h_0^*J\to K$ and hence $h_0^*:H^2(X_0,J)\to H^2(Y_0,K)$. For every line module $L$ on $X_0$, one has $\delta_Y(h_0^*L)=h_0^*\delta_X(L)$. No cartesianness or flatness of this square is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DNM, lemma-picard-group-first-order-thickening, exact sequence and proof via a -> 1+a; pullback naturality is the naturality of that units exact sequence and its connecting map.

proof.text: Identify $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $X_{0,\mathrm{et}}$ using the first-order ringed description. Use the enlarged etale site, whose final object is $X_0$, when evaluating global sections; restriction to scheme charts is a ringed-topos equivalence. Such an equivalence preserves injectives and sections, so it identifies the derived global sections. On this common topos put $R=\mathcal O_X$ and $A=\mathcal O_{X_0}$. The ring extension $0\to J\to R\to A\to0$ gives the short exact sequence of abelian sheaves $S_X:0\to J\xrightarrow{j\mapsto1+j}R^\times\to A^\times\to0$. Indeed $(1+j)(1+j')=1+j+j'$ and $(1+j)^{-1}=1-j$. Its kernel consists exactly of these elements. A local unit $a$ in $A$ and its inverse lift locally to $r,s$ in $R$; if $rs=1+t$ with $t\in J$, then $r$ is a unit with inverse $s(1-t)$. Thus surjectivity is sheaf-local, not an assertion about surjectivity on global units.

Abelian sheaves on this small site have enough injectives. Apply the horseshoe delta-functor theorem to the additive left exact functor of global sections and $S_X$. It gives an exact segment $H^1(R^\times)\to H^1(A^\times)\xrightarrow{\partial_X}H^2(J)$. Let $c_R,c_A$ be the canonical Picard--$H^1$ isomorphisms and define $\delta_X=\partial_Xc_A$. Naturality of those isomorphisms for the quotient ringed-topos morphism identifies $H^1(R^\times)\to H^1(A^\times)$ with restriction $\operatorname{Pic}(X)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X_0)$. Therefore $\delta_X$ is a group homomorphism and its kernel is exactly the stated image. Independence of horseshoe resolutions makes the boundary canonical; the site equivalence introduces no choice in the transported map. The same construction defines $\delta_Y$.

proof.text: For the square in the statement, the canonical etale ringed-topos morphisms and their composition comparisons identify the map induced by $h$ on the common topoi with the one induced by $h_0$. Write $q:h_0^{-1}R\to\mathcal O_Y$ for its ring map and $\bar q:h_0^{-1}A\to\mathcal O_{Y_0}$ for its quotient. Since the square commutes, $q$ sends $h_0^{-1}J$ into $K$; denote this additive map by $\alpha$. Its $h_0^{-1}A$-linearity follows because two lifts of a scalar differ by an element mapped into $K$, and $K^2=0$. Thus its extension of scalars is precisely $h_0^*J\to K$, $a\otimes j\mapsto\widetilde a\,q(j)$. The equality $q(1+j)=1+\alpha(j)$ and compatibility with quotient maps give a morphism of short exact sequences $h_0^{-1}S_X\to S_Y$ with end maps $\alpha$ and $\rho:h_0^{-1}A^\times\to\mathcal O_{Y_0}^\times$. This is a map from inverse images of additive sheaves; no tensor-exactness assertion is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DNM, units-sequence construction, applied functorially to the given square

proof.text: The site-cohomology pullback theorem gives $h_0^*\partial_X=\partial_{h_0^{-1}S_X}h_0^*$. Here $V=X_0$ is the final object of the enlarged site of $X_0$ and $u(V)=Y_0\times_{X_0}X_0=Y_0$ is final in that of $Y_0$, so global sections are evaluation at these objects and $\Gamma(X_0,h_{0*}G)=G(Y_0)$; the defining formula $\Gamma(V,\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\eta}\Gamma(u(V),h_0^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\beta}\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J^\bullet)$ of this $h_0^*$ is therefore literally the defining formula of the map $h_0^*$ in the Picard--$H^1$ comparison, so the same $h_0^*$ appears in both. Apply naturality of the horseshoe connecting maps on $Y_0$ to the morphism of sequences from step 3: $H^2(\alpha)\partial_{h_0^{-1}S_X}=\partial_YH^1(\rho)$. Combining these equalities gives $H^2(\alpha)h_0^*\partial_X=\partial_YH^1(\rho)h_0^*$. The new ringed-site Picard--$H^1$ comparison gives $H^1(\rho)h_0^*c_A([L])=c_{\mathcal O_{Y_0}}([h_0^*L])$. Substitution yields $h_0^*\delta_X([L])=\delta_Y([h_0^*L])$, where the map on $H^2$ is exactly pullback on abelian sheaves followed by $H^2(\alpha)$, hence is the coefficient map specified in the statement. All pullbacks used on short exact sequences were inverse images of abelian sheaves, which are exact for every morphism of sites; no cartesianness or flatness was used.
